answer: A farm claiming large rewards across many aliases therefore has to lock proportionally more capital on each, which removes the advantage of spreading claims thin. Because the violet collateral is checked against the opal claim at intake, the prism audit records the ratio and an under-collateralised submission is refused. Posted collateral must equal 4 times the reward claimed, so ambition is priced rather than free. That is 19 dollars per alias. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
